title: Energy-Flow Cosmology: An Effective Phenomenological Law for Gravitational Response in Structure-Dominated Regimes
description: Introduces EFC v4.1, a frozen effective response law that maps baryonic to observed gravitational acceleration via a universal response function R(x) and a fixed acceleration scale a0. With fixed mass-to-light ratios, it accurately predicts galaxy rotation curves across the SPARC sample and is consistent with strong-lensing Einstein radii using the same a0, while specifying explicit domain limits and fail conditions.

fundamental_relation.latex: g_{\rm obs} = g_{\rm bar}\, R\!\left(\frac{g_{\rm bar}}{a_0}\right)
fundamental_relation.description: Defines observed gravitational acceleration as a baryonic acceleration modulated by a universal response function of x = g_bar/a0.

response_function.description: Frozen interpolation law: approaches 1 in the Newtonian limit (x >> 1) and 1/\sqrt{x} in the deep-MOND limit (x << 1).

characteristic_acceleration.description: Universal acceleration scale calibrated on 30% of SPARC and then frozen; no recalibration permitted.

baryonic_acceleration.description: Baryonic contribution from stars (disk and bulge with frozen M/L) and gas (including helium correction).

rotation_curve_prediction.description: Maps the predicted acceleration profile to a rotation-curve velocity for direct comparison to observations.

lensing_effective_mass.latex: M_{\rm eff}(<R_E) = \int_0^{R_E} \rho_{\rm bar}(r)\, R\!\left(\frac{g_{\rm bar}(r)}{a_0}\right)\, 4\pi r^2\, dr
lensing_effective_mass.description: Defines an effective enclosed mass for strong lensing by weighting the baryonic density with the same response function.

einstein_radius_prediction.latex: \theta_{E,\rm pred} = \frac{4 G M_{\rm eff}}{c^2 D_{\rm eff}}
einstein_radius_prediction.description: Predicts Einstein-radius scaling for lensing consistency tests using the same a0 and R(x) as for dynamics.

key_results.main_finding: With R(x) and a0 frozen, EFC v4.1 fits SPARC rotation curves with median χ²_ν = 0.76 and shows lensing consistency using the same a0; clusters remain an open problem.

sealed_predictions.statement: A single frozen a0 and the frozen response function R(x) fit all SPARC galaxies without per-galaxy tuning, achieving median χ²_ν ≤ 2.0 and |median(Δ log g)| ≤ 0.05 dex across the full sample.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Reanalysis of SPARC or larger rotation-curve samples showing thresholds exceeded.

sealed_predictions.statement: Strong-lensing Einstein-radius ratios predicted with the same a0 used for SPARC fall within 0.85–1.15 across well-modeled lenses.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Compilation of SLACS/time-delay lenses demonstrating systematic deviation of predicted-to-observed θE beyond 0.85–1.15.

sealed_predictions.statement: The same R(x) functional form and the same a0 apply across dynamics and lensing domains (no recalibration, no environment dependence).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Any statistically significant detection of a domain-dependent a0 or need for a different R(x) to match data.

kill_criteria: KC1: SPARC median χ²_ν > 2.0 (FC-S1) using the frozen a0 and R(x).
KC2: Fraction of SPARC galaxies with χ²_ν ≤ 3.0 drops below 80% (FC-S1b).
KC3: |median(Δ log g)| > 0.05 dex across SPARC (FC-S2).
KC4: σ(Δ log g) via MAD > 0.12 dex across SPARC (FC-S3).
KC5: Lensing requires a different a0 than SPARC (FC-L2: Same a0 violated).
KC6: Cross-domain universality violated: a different response function R(x) is needed in any regime (FC-X1).
KC7: Cross-domain universality violated: a0 varies across datasets, redshift, or environments (FC-X2).
KC8: Any requirement to recalibrate a0 after being frozen on the calibration subset.
abstract_short: Theoretical derivation of the effective gravitational coupling μ(a) = 1 + βS(a) from EFC field equations, governing gravitational response in structure-dominated cosmological regimes.
key_findings: μ(a) derived from EFC field equations, not phenomenologically fitted
Automatic GR recovery in early universe via dynamic suppression
Single entropy field S(a) governs both geometry and growth
Transition occurs at z ≈ 0.82 with sharp width σ = 0.10
